Doorman.existing: The doorway rank and craft. Gerk is treated as the prophesied Doorman; Carlkin withholds the title.
notes: Carlkin treats the practice as rules worth writing down. Do not open a doorway on a moving thing. Do not open a door to an unknown place. Opening with no destination opens onto nowhere: the nothing, the astral, or the gap between arches. Correct use is to picture one specific familiar door and open it as if by hand.

A portal on a moving ship stays fixed and can tear reality or become a three-way connection. Mastery and wide travel could allow openings nearly anywhere, but a keystone-bound Doorman should expect requests tied to that keystone.
Other people besides Gerk can open doors. Carlkin does not name them. A keystone is generally used by a gatekeeper or a doorman. Long study, or a purpose-built gate, can work around that.

Doorman is the rank above footman. Doormen were the more prestigious rank and taught footmen, their apprentices. Carlkin will not grant Gerk the Doorman title yet and calls him a footman until he earns it. The legends, as Carlkin tells them, treat the role as Gerk's own choice. Sylan is the one who identified him and brought him the news.
openQuestions: Who are the other doormen, and does Carlkin know them?

Gatekeeper.existing: The role of holding a keystone for an Arch realm and managing paths between realms.
notes: Dana says the party are all gatekeepers now. Carlkin accepts that and treats it as a larger responsibility than opening doors casually. He says they have pledged themselves to the role.

A gatekeeper can do more than open a fixed door. Opening one functional gatehouse connects it to the other functional arch gatehouses at once, in a web, regardless of who is present. Carlkin's corrected count is the other seven. That chaining is a property of gatehouses on ley lines. A keystone used elsewhere still needs a powerful ley-line crossing.
When every keystone is assembled in one gatehouse, the gatekeepers must largely stay there, dormant, and keep the gate safe. Except for Gerk, the party has not successfully opened a keystone portal.

Mother's Prayer.existing: Ancient Navi prophecy that currently describes Gerk.
notes: Sylan describes it to Carlkin as an ancient prophecy that made the party more important after they finished bringing the keystones to Juten Prime, with Gerk as the one who matters. Carlkin asks whether it is about Gerk, and Sylan says it would seem so.

Carlkin had not been told. He connects it at once to Gerk being an orphan who sees things, calls it an interesting conundrum studied by several scholars, and says Gerk is subject to the whims of the universe because of it. He refuses to name those scholars and keeps part of what he knows in reserve.

He treats Gerk holding or being subject to the Mother's Prayer as part of why Gerk is the Doorman, and he implies that entanglement with it would eventually have revealed the role even without Sylan's investigation.
openQuestions: Which scholars study it, and what is Carlkin refusing to say?

Al Kurin.existing: Vessels containing the souls of dragons.
notes: Carlkin treats Grixto's dragon-killing as theft of Al Kurin and immediately asks where Walker and his dragon are. Elrus says Walker's theory, that Grixto became a lich after Galixtar's death, would explain his eagerness to obtain the Al Kurin.

Lines of magic that gatehouses sit on. Carlkin says a keystone portal opened away from a gatehouse would need a powerful crossing of them. The party has tried and, apart from Gerk's doors, has not succeeded.
Four landscape carvings in the roost cave show the largest landmark to the east, west, north, and south, each a mountain or an island, as seen from the ruined tower.

Each is a small number of degrees off the cardinal bearing where it should sit. The western one is drawn like a clock hand that has slipped from nine o'clock toward nine-twenty or nine-thirty. Elrus cannot make the angles fit a single vantage and attributes them to Grixto carving from a faulty memory.
Walker believes matching the real landscape to that tilt will point toward a place to go or a thing to find. An investigation from the tower was called and not resolved.
openQuestions: Does rotating to match the tilted drawings point to a destination or another clue?

notes: Vecna's term for gods who did not originate in Atlas. He says they came from other pantheons, brought by other creatures. He sets himself apart from them as Atlas-born, and says he is a demigod rather than an elder.

Abyssal eye-beast.existing: The oily tentacled, many-eyed creature the party just fought through the lighthouse door.
notes: The fight was loud enough to wake Benji. Carlkin still describes the place beyond the door as hell, or nearly hell. With the door closed, the creature is gone from the lighthouse.
Carlkin says it almost used his living room as a birthing place. He thinks the aimless door opened between the arches and that this was probably an astral being rather than simply an abomination.

Keystone Keepers.existing: The party members entrusted with keystones and realms, recognized as children of the Great Eldarin Tree.
notes: They have pledged themselves as gatekeepers. Carlkin treats that pledge, alongside the Doorman, as the normal license to use a keystone, with long study as a lesser workaround.

If every keystone is assembled in a single gatehouse, he says they are more or less obligated to remain there, dormant, and protect it. Except for Gerk, they have not successfully opened a keystone portal.
Grixto had captured them by the time the party first killed him. The party searched for where he was keeping them, suspected Gilbrick, and on going there found him for the second fight.

Navi.existing: Ancient race tied to the Eldarin Tree, the keystones, and the Mother's Prayer.
notes: Vecna says he is not of the Navi line. He claims the first peoples of Atlas as his own stock. The name was heard as Narvi.

newTerms.name: Between arches
notes: Carlkin's name for where a door opened with no destination goes. He equates that door to nowhere with the nothing, the astral sea, or the space between arches. The lighthouse creature came from there and nearly used the room as a birthing place.

newTerms.name: Three-way portal
notes: A failure mode Carlkin describes when portal magic is used on a moving object: the portal can stay fixed, reality can rip, and the opening can connect more than the intended two places.

newTerms.name: Assembled gatehouse dormancy
notes: Carlkin's claim that once all keystones sit in one gate or gatehouse, the gatekeepers are obliged to remain there and keep the hub safe rather than travel freely.

newTerms.name: Footman
notes: Carlkin's name for an apprentice doorman. Doormen were more prestigious and taught footmen the craft. He uses the rank for Gerk until Gerk earns Doorman.

newTerms.name: Ley line
notes: Lines of magic that gatehouses sit on, which is why opening one functional arch gatehouse opens the other functional ones together. Carlkin says a keystone portal away from a gatehouse would need a powerful ley-line crossing.

newTerms.name: Emperor of Nyx
notes: Title of the hobgoblin emperor, which Carlkin recognizes. Sylan identifies him with the lich Grixto, also called Emperor of the Hobgoblins and remembered as Garixto. His fall threw the hobgoblins into civil war.

newTerms.name: Sylan's sister
notes: Sylan hopes to bring her home and suggests that doing so may turn out well. No name or location is given.

newTerms.name: Raskina
notes: Vecna's red-skinned book, also called the Book of Vecna. Misheard as Redskina, ratskin, Rayaskina, and Rexkina. Pages are his sister Valkyrie's skin and the ink is her blood. Vecna cast the runes and did not fill the pages; the text wrote itself, which he attributes to the void and demons.

The powerful spellbook Grixto found when he turned from dragon rider to hunter of dragon riders. Dana says Grixto has it, Walker says the lich allegedly has it, and it appears in Emhet's vision of the young lich. Vecna wants it back. An elder of his showed the party a vision of its last known location, and he offers boons or a deal to whoever finds it. A listener fears its darkness may have brought down their order.

Walker and Vecna agree it is not Grixto's phylactery, though Vecna once hypothesized that it might be and Walker said he would destroy it if it were. Vecna claims it can seek that phylactery and restore lost people, things, or beings. A miniature copy and a red quill let Walker write to him.

newTerms.name: Twin Bloody Comet
notes: Reach cautionary legend for the pairing of Garixto the Betrayer and the red dragon Galixtar, taught to dragon-rider trainees of other guilds.

newTerms.name: Heart of hearts
notes: In the Twin Bloody Comet warning, something a dragon gives only to the bonded rider, and only when death is inevitable. Dragons who lost their riders mourned that they had not given it.

newTerms.name: Council of Nyx
notes: Captives Grixto, as Garixto, was holding when the party first killed him. Searching for them led the party through the arches to Gilbrick, where they found him instead.

newTerms.name: Grixto's helmet
notes: Taken by Walker off the lich and still worn as a style choice. Leading suspect for the mundane phylactery.

newTerms.name: Garixto the Betrayer
notes: The name under which Grixto is remembered in Reach dragon-rider legend, paired with the red dragon Galixtar as the Twin Bloody Comet.

newTerms.name: Vecna's elder
notes: Vecna credits an elder of his with the vision of the Raskina's last known location that the party was shown.

newTerms.name: Voyager gods
notes: Vecna's term for gods who did not originate in Atlas and were brought from other pantheons, like vermin on ships. He contrasts them with himself, a demigod born in Atlas. The phrase may be misheard.

newTerms.name: Valkyrie
notes: Vecna's sister and, in his telling, one of the first shield maidens. He killed her and used her skin and blood to make the Raskina. He says the name survived only as a watered-down legend.

newTerms.name: Orcus
notes: Demon prince Vecna says holds some claim on the domain of the undead alongside his own. Heard as Orcas.

newTerms.name: Guild stronghold ruins
notes: Cliffside ruins of the dragon-rider guild stronghold from Elrus and Grixto's past, above the roost cave. Average stronghold scale, with dragon housing, a cliffside stable once joined by a covered walkway that has fallen, and a central tower about eighty feet across, now low walls and overgrowth. The cave carvings copy the view from that tower, which Walker also knows from the training yard.

newTerms.name: Dragon-rider madness
notes: Elrus says madness is the most common outcome when either a dragon or its rider dies, severe enough that the survivor might seek a book to bring the other back.

newTerms.name: Tilted landmarks
notes: Cardinal mountains or islands carved on the cave wall a few degrees off their true bearings, as seen from the ruined tower. Walker is treating the offset as a directional clue.
